retired.elevation.hills: An absolute cut on the elevation field. Replaced by elevation.hillShare: hills are now the flank band of the relief field, sized as a share of land.
retired.elevation.mountains: An absolute cut on the elevation field, which made blob mountains wherever the continental noise happened to peak. Replaced by elevation.mountainShare, a quantile of a ridged relief field whose crests are lines.
retired.noise.moisture: A single-scale moisture field, which dusted forest evenly over every continent. Replaced by noise.moistureRegional times noise.moistureLocal — see moisture.regionalWeight.
retired.moisture.forestMin: An absolute moisture cut for forest. Replaced by moisture.forestShare: the moisture field decides *where* the wood is, a share of eligible ground decides how much.
retired.moisture.jungleMin: The same cut for jungle, which asked whether a tropical tile was wetter than most of the *world* — so a seed whose wet regions missed the equator had no jungle at all. Replaced by moisture.jungleShare, ranked inside the band.
retired.rivers.maxAttempts: A flat cap on springs examined. Replaced by rivers.attemptsPerRiver: the budget has to scale with the quota it serves, or the largest maps come up short of rivers.
retired.resources.countPer1000LandTiles: One purse for every resource, split by frequency weight, so retuning bonus density silently retuned strategic scarcity. Replaced by resources.bonusPer1000LandTiles and resources.strategicPer1000LandTiles; luxuries left the purse entirely and are dealt per continent.
retired.resources.luxuryKindsPerRegion: A hand per connected landmass, which on a one-continent map was one hand for the world. Replaced by resources.luxuryKindsPerContinent over the fixed-size continents of carveContinents.
